description: This topic explores the different sources historians use to reconstruct the past, including archaeology, oral traditions, written records, archives, museums, audio-visual materials and linguistics, along with their advantages, limitations and methods of preservation.

mcq.questionText: Which source of historical information depends mainly on the study of materials dug from the ground, such as fossils, bones and tools?
mcq.explanation: Archaeology is the scientific study of material remains such as fossils, bones and tools that are excavated from the ground.

mcq.questionText: A story about the origin of a clan that an elder tells to his grandchildren by word of mouth is an example of which source of history?
mcq.explanation: Oral tradition refers to information passed by word of mouth from one generation to another, such as stories, songs and proverbs.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the BEST example of a written source of historical information?

options.text: A pot found during an excavation
A traditional dance performed at a festival
An old letter written by a colonial officer
A wooden spear kept in a museum

mcq.explanation: Written sources include letters, diaries, books and official documents that record events in writing.

mcq.questionText: A building or institution where historical documents and government records are officially kept for safekeeping and reference is called a/an:
mcq.explanation: An archive is a place where original documents and records are preserved so that they can be used by researchers in the future.

mcq.questionText: Which source of historical information uses the study of languages to trace the relationships and migrations of different peoples?
mcq.explanation: Linguistics studies languages and their similarities, which can show how peoples are related and how they migrated in the past.

mcq.questionText: Films, recorded sound and photographs that capture past events belong to which category of historical sources?
mcq.explanation: Audio-visual sources are materials that can be heard and seen, such as films, photographs and sound recordings.

mcq.questionText: What is the main scientific method used to estimate the age of very old fossils and remains found by archaeologists?
mcq.explanation: Carbon dating is a scientific method that measures the remaining carbon in organic remains to estimate their age.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major LIMITATION of oral tradition as a source of history?

options.text: It is too expensive to collect
Information may be distorted or exaggerated as it is passed on
It can only be used by scientists
It requires reading and writing skills

mcq.explanation: Because oral tradition is passed by word of mouth, details can be forgotten, changed or exaggerated over time.

mcq.questionText: Which institution preserves and displays historical objects such as artefacts, tools and bones so that the public can see and learn from them?
mcq.explanation: A museum collects, preserves and exhibits objects of historical, cultural and scientific importance for public viewing.

mcq.questionText: One important advantage of written sources over oral traditions is that written sources:

options.text: Can be remembered without any record
Are never biased in any way
Can be stored and referred to exactly as they were recorded

mcq.explanation: Written records keep information in a fixed form that can be read again later, unlike oral information that may change over time.

mcq.questionText: Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania is famous in history mainly because it is an important site for which type of source?
mcq.explanation: Olduvai Gorge is an important archaeological site where ancient fossils and stone tools of early humans have been discovered.

mcq.questionText: Why might a written record left by a colonial government be considered a biased source of history?

options.text: Because it was written in ink
Because it reflects the views and interests of the colonisers
Because it was kept in an archive

mcq.explanation: Documents written by colonisers often present events from their own point of view, which can give a one-sided picture of the past.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the relationship between archaeology and written records as sources of history?

options.text: Archaeology can provide information about periods before writing was invented
Written records are always older than archaeological remains
Archaeology and written records cannot be used together
Written records are only useful for the Stone Age

mcq.explanation: Archaeology is especially valuable for studying the distant past before people knew how to write, when no written records exist.

mcq.questionText: A historian wants to study how the Bantu peoples spread across East Africa long ago. Which source would be MOST useful for tracing this movement through word similarities?
mcq.explanation: Linguistics compares languages and shared words to trace migrations and connections between peoples such as the Bantu.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly explains why historians prefer to use more than one source of information when studying the past?

options.text: It makes the work take longer
Different sources can be compared to check facts and reduce errors
It is required only for museums

mcq.explanation: Using several sources allows a historian to cross-check information so that mistakes and bias in one source can be corrected.

fib.questionText: The study of material remains such as fossils and tools dug from the ground is called _____.
fib.explanation: Archaeology recovers and studies physical remains of the past from the earth.

fib.questionText: Information that is passed from one generation to another by word of mouth is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Oral tradition includes spoken stories, songs and proverbs handed down over time.

fib.questionText: A place where original documents and government records are officially kept and preserved is called an _____.
fib.explanation: Archives store original records so they can be consulted by researchers in the future.

fib.questionText: An institution that collects, preserves and displays historical objects for the public is a _____.
fib.explanation: Museums exhibit artefacts and remains so people can view and learn from them.

fib.questionText: The branch of knowledge that studies languages to trace the relationships and migrations of peoples is called _____.
fib.explanation: Linguistics uses similarities between languages to reveal historical links between peoples.

fib.questionText: Films, photographs and recorded sound are grouped together as _____ sources of history.
fib.explanation: Audio-visual sources are materials that can be both heard and seen.

fib.questionText: The scientific method used to estimate the age of organic remains by measuring carbon is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Carbon dating measures remaining carbon in once-living material to estimate its age.

fib.questionText: Letters, diaries, books and official documents are examples of _____ sources of historical information.
fib.explanation: Written sources record events using letters and symbols on a surface.

fib.questionText: The remains of dead plants or animals that have hardened in rock over a very long time are called _____.
fib.explanation: Fossils are preserved remains studied by archaeologists to learn about very ancient life.

fib.questionText: Keeping historical materials safe from damage, theft and decay so they last for the future is called _____ of historical information.
fib.explanation: Preservation protects sources such as documents and artefacts so future generations can use them.

tf.questionText: Archaeology can provide information about periods of history that happened before writing was invented.
tf.explanation: Because archaeology studies physical remains, it can reveal the distant past even when no written records exist.

tf.questionText: Oral tradition can never be changed or exaggerated as it is passed from one generation to another.
tf.explanation: Oral tradition can be forgotten, distorted or exaggerated over time, which is one of its main limitations.

tf.questionText: An archive and a museum are exactly the same kind of institution.
tf.explanation: An archive mainly keeps documents and records, while a museum mainly collects and displays objects and artefacts.

tf.questionText: Written sources of history can sometimes be biased because they reflect the views of the people who wrote them.
tf.explanation: Authors may record events from their own point of view, so written sources are not always neutral.

tf.questionText: Linguistics helps historians by comparing languages to discover how different peoples are related.
tf.explanation: Similarities between languages can show migrations and connections between groups of people.

tf.questionText: Photographs and films are useless as sources of historical information.
tf.explanation: Audio-visual materials such as photographs and films can record real events and are valuable historical sources.

tf.questionText: Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania is an important archaeological site for studying early human history.
tf.explanation: Olduvai Gorge has yielded many fossils and stone tools of early humans, making it a key archaeological site.

tf.questionText: Using only one source of historical information is the most reliable way to study the past.
tf.explanation: Historians use several sources together so that they can cross-check facts and reduce errors and bias.

tf.questionText: Carbon dating is a method used to estimate the age of old organic remains.
tf.explanation: Carbon dating measures the carbon remaining in once-living material to estimate how old it is.

tf.questionText: Preservation of historical information is not necessary because sources can never be destroyed.
tf.explanation: Sources can decay, be damaged or be lost, so preservation is needed to keep them for the future.

summary.correctAnswer: Any material or evidence used to obtain information about the past.
summary.explanation: Sources provide the evidence historians use to reconstruct past events.

summary.correctAnswer: Studying material remains such as fossils, bones and tools dug from the ground.
summary.explanation: Archaeology focuses on physical evidence recovered from the earth.

summary.correctAnswer: Information passed by word of mouth from one generation to another.
summary.explanation: It includes stories, songs, proverbs and legends spoken aloud.

summary.correctAnswer: Letters, diaries, books and official documents.
summary.explanation: These record events in writing and can be read again later.

summary.questionText: Difference between an archive and a museum
summary.correctAnswer: Archives keep documents and records, while museums display objects and artefacts.
summary.explanation: Both preserve the past but handle different types of material.

summary.correctAnswer: It compares languages to trace relationships and migrations of peoples.
summary.explanation: Shared words and structures reveal historical links between groups.

summary.correctAnswer: Materials that can be heard and seen, such as films, photographs and recordings.
summary.explanation: They capture events in sound and pictures.

summary.correctAnswer: They store information in a fixed form that can be referred to later.
summary.explanation: This makes them more permanent than spoken information.

summary.explanation: Word of mouth depends on memory, which can change details.

summary.questionText: Why preservation of historical information matters
summary.correctAnswer: It keeps sources safe from decay, damage and loss for future use.
summary.explanation: Preserved sources allow future generations to study the past.

hoq.questionText: A researcher finds that an oral tradition and a written colonial record describe the same battle very differently. What is the BEST approach for the historian to take?

options.text: Accept the written record because it is written down
Compare both sources critically and look for additional evidence to judge what likely happened
Accept the oral tradition because it is older

hoq.explanation: When sources disagree, a historian critically compares them and seeks more evidence rather than trusting one source blindly.

hoq.questionText: Why might archaeology be considered MORE reliable than oral tradition for studying events that happened thousands of years ago?

options.text: Because physical remains are not affected by human memory and can be dated scientifically
Because archaeology is cheaper than collecting stories
Because oral tradition only exists in towns

hoq.explanation: Material remains do not depend on memory and can be dated with scientific methods, making them reliable for the very distant past.

hoq.questionText: A community wants to make sure its history survives even if its elders pass away. Which combination of actions would BEST preserve this history?

options.text: Only telling the stories to children
Recording the elders on audio-visual devices and writing the stories down for an archive
Waiting for archaeologists to dig later

hoq.explanation: Recording elders and writing the stories for safekeeping turns fragile oral tradition into more permanent, preserved sources.
